title: AS//0 - Persistent Multiplayer 4X Strategy Cyber/Hacking Sim
author: Downtown_Ad_1119
selftext:
Currently in Beta (keys available) and looking for feedback on everything down to whether or not it looks fun.  Contact info available in comments.

**Autonomous System Zero (AS//0)** is a persistent multiplayer cyberwar strategy game built around a playable terminal. Its systems include:

* **Network construction and defense:** Build layered networks with firewalls, trace systems, ICE, storage, traps, and specialized infrastructure.
* **Resource heists:** Infiltrate other networks to steal bytes, hardware, and money. Your own networks don’t passively farm resources—you have to go get them.
* **Recon and filesystem exploration:** Search directories, read logs, and uncover metadata, bypass information, and credentials.
* **Timed infiltration:** Work through network layers, defeat interactive ICE encounters, and decide how much you can accomplish before the trace catches you.
* **Uncertain targets:** Player and NPC networks share the world. You may need deeper reconnaissance to discover whose network you’re breaking into.
* **Network capture:** Steal entire networks and expand your operation across multiple locations.
* **Exploit crafting and loadouts:** Collect fragments, craft tools, and prepare exploits for the operation you’re planning.
* **Active countermeasures:** Set traps and deploy defensive exploits against intruders while they’re inside your network.
* **International operations:** Explore countries, navigate border security, establish gateways, and connect networks through VPNs.
* **Collectives and shared infrastructure:** Form groups with membership roles, permissions, headquarters, and a shared vault for stockpiling resources and tools.
* **Communication and espionage:** Coordinate through chat and mail, send attachments, monitor friendly networks, and intercept enemy communications.
* **Netfall endgame:** A collective survival showdown where preparation, infrastructure, and alliances are put to the test.

The idea is that a routine resource run can become reconnaissance, a capture attempt, or the beginning of a rivalry—and a difficult target can become a coordinated heist.

Developer disclaimer:

Every thoughtful vision, intertwining system, clever mechanic, immersion technique, canon translation, and design decision are ENTIRELY MINE.

AI (including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Suno) assisted with coding, syntax, brainstorming, balancing calculations, graphic generation, music generation, and API integration.  
Lets be clear, the game WORKS because of AI, it is FUN because of ME.

That being said, I would like to explain HOW I got generative AI to help me create such a complex game and not work against itself or me.  (I primarily use ChatGPT.  References are to ChatGPT's capability)

First, have a long conversation about:

* What you want to make
* Why you want to make it
* What inspired you
* Other games you can draw ideas from
* What you imagine it to look like
* What systems you want to include by havent even considered how yet

Basically, just brainstorm with the AI, and when you are finished ask it to compose a "vision document" that sums up everything you talked about no matter how insignificant.

Start a project and include the vision doc in the sources.  When you start a conversation, ask the AI to read the document before you start.

As you start making the game, dont let conversations get too long, token overlap can be a real problem.  After you have a few things made, ask the AI to create a "current features document" that summarizes everything you have implemented so far.  

I started by using a zip file that I would overwrite and extract each time changes were made.  This worked well, but connecting a github repo can really improve the workflow process.  But, no matter which, when starting a new conversation upload the current zip file and the most recent current features document.  

Now each conversation begins with: 

"The zip (or repo) is the most recent build and current progress on the project.  The current features document outlines the details of implemented mechanics.  The original design document is for vision only."  

This works great for the work mode that doesn't converse the same as the chat mode does.  The AI will create a heirachy of what takes precedence when making desing implementations. This saved me many headaches about reminding the AI where we were in the project, correcting when it tried to use something we decided to omit, or having to roll back changes that dont follow the design principles.  

Hopefully this helps anyone trying to solo a complex development.  Please check out my game and tell me what you think.
